newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia's Samper calls summit to end guerrilla war.
newsitem.headline: Colombia's Samper calls summit to end guerrilla war.

text.p: Colombian President Ernesto Samper said on Friday he would call a "peace summit" after Easter to try to end three decades of guerrilla warfare.
"I will call a peace summit...so that we can work on a solution to end this bloodshed," Samper said in the southwest city of Popayan. He set no date.
Last week, Samper's newly-appointed Defence Minister Gilberto Echeverri called for fresh efforts to find a peaceful solution to a guerrilla uprising by three armed leftist groups.
The Maoist People's Liberation Army (EPL), whose members have mostly laid down their arms, said it was ready to talk.

But the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC), Latin America's oldest and largest rebel group, and the Cuban-inspired National Liberation Army (ELN), have not given clear signs they would take part in exploratory peace talks.

Political analysts doubt whether Colombia's armed forces will want to sit down at the same table with the rebels. Much of the military top-brass are convinced they can defeat the guerrillas if they are given more troops and equipment.

In previous peace processes begun in the 1980s the leftist M-19 guerrilla group and much of the EPL laid down their guns. Both groups were considered to have been militarily defeated by the time they demobilized in the late 1980s and early 1990s.
The FARC and the ELN, in contrast, appear to be at one of their strongest points since they were formed in the mid-1960s.
The FARC launched a bloody offensive in August and the ELN recently staged a wave of car-bomb attacks in eastern Colombia.
In the northwest banana-growing region of Uraba, meanwhile, military sources said at least four FARC guerrillas had been killed in fighting since Thursday.
